A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MS-HAB benchmark. Their complete main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite figure renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulator benchmarks, RL and IL success rates, and appendix experiments on dataset size, collision thresholds, algorithm choice, and policy failure modes.

after.justification: v3 retains these original policy experiments and appendix analyses, alongside revised simulator throughput and memory measurements.

M1.justification: The documented environment design, controls, learning architectures, skill chaining, and trajectory-filtering procedure remain unchanged. Revised simulator performance measurements do not establish an algorithm or component change.

E1.justification: Both versions use ReplicaCAD scenes, YCB objects, and Fetch for TidyHouse, PrepareGroceries, and SetTable. The Interact, ray-tracing, simplified-task, and collision-threshold scenarios are retained; no new dataset or task coverage is introduced.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Habitat in the Interact benchmark, Behavior-1k in Appendix A.5, and the RL-Per/RL-All/IL, SAC/PPO, and BC/diffusion-policy comparisons. Diffusion-policy results already appear in v1 Table 5.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 extends the MS-HAB concurrency sweep beyond 1024 environments to include 2048 and 4096. Appendix A.5 changes the reported ray-tracing GPU from RTX 3070 to RTX 4090. Policy training budgets, splits, metrics, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The per-object policy and demonstration-filtering ablations are retained, as are the appendix analyses of dataset size, task simplification, SAC versus PPO, collision thresholds, and failure modes. Their evidence is unchanged; the simulator benchmark revisions add no separate diagnostic analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain ten benchmarking seeds/runs with 95% confidence intervals, three RL training seeds, and min/max bands for learning curves. Changed uncertainty values in Appendix A.5 do not change the statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Changes are confined to simulator benchmarks. Section 4.2 revises the speed/memory curve and reports 4299.18 SPS at 4096 environments instead of 4109.40 at 1024, changing the Habitat speed ratio from 2.94x to 3.08x. Under Appendix A.5's changed GPU, MS-HAB/Behavior-1k throughput becomes 69.90/19.92 rather than 60.42/15.56 SPS, and memory becomes 6.26/7.62 rather than 4.01/5.96 GB. These are revised measurements under changed configurations, not same-setting gains. Policy tables and learning curves are unchanged.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation, subtask success conditions, initialization definitions, and formal trajectory-event/category definitions in Section 3 and Appendices A.1, A.2, and A.6 are unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction strengthen the efficiency claim from approximately threefold speed at similar GPU memory to threefold speed at a fraction of the memory; the advertised throughput also changes from over 4000 to over 4300 SPS. The benchmark, baseline, filtering, and data-generation contributions retain their original scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 adds a less efficient renderer to the explanation of Habitat's performance limitations, previously attributed to CPU parallelization. Interpretations of policy failures, filtering behavior, and applicability limitations, including the absence of real-robot transfer claims, remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 9 changes dataset availability from a 490 GB upload still in progress to a reported public release through the project website. The front matter explicitly lists models among available resources, and Appendix A.5 updates the GPU identification. Other implementation details remain stable.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive related-work discussion in Section 2 are retained. The bibliography removes many URL fields without removing the corresponding works or revising the novelty positioning.

P1.justification: Most prose and the section hierarchy remain intact. Limited edits include the conference-publication header, revised benchmarking and reproducibility paragraphs, punctuation changes, and an added cross-reference from Appendix A.3 to A.4.4.

P2.justification: v3 adds a four-scene ray-traced montage as Figure 1 and updates the Interact plot and caption as Figure 2, including additional concurrency labels. Existing figures are renumbered or relocated, tables reflow, and links and headers receive presentation changes; the remaining scientific displays are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves usability and reporting: Section 9 replaces a pending dataset upload with a reported public release, while Section 4.2 extends the concurrency sweep and explicitly quantifies peak memory use. The new overview figure also illustrates the environments. These gains are limited because methods, policy results, and diagnostic analyses remain unchanged; the changed hardware in Appendix A.5 prevents treating its higher throughput as a version-to-version performance improvement.
